paper_verdict.estimator_family: system GMM (Blundell-Bond), collapsed instruments, robust SE
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: All main-effect coefficients (DE, cell phone, internet user, broadband) are conditional on interaction with ln human capital (effect at H=0), so they are negative while interactions are positive; not comparable to unconditional effects. DE is a PCA index (unit-free) and component variables are ratios, with very different scales (broadband -4.796). Text says N=54 countries but tables use 41 countries, 779 obs. Estimates from the same sample are not independent. Reverse causality: authors cite mutual causation as motive for system GMM, but give no further tests (Hansen and AR tests only).

estimates.note: Table 2 col (4); note says robust standard errors in brackets. Main DE term in a model with DE x ln H interaction, so it is the effect at H=0 (conditional), not an average effect. Dependent var is lnGDP per capita with lagged term.
Table 2 col (4); interaction coefficient, not a marginal effect.
Table 2 col (1); conditional on interaction with human capital.
Table 2 col (3); fixed broadband; coefficient scale differs greatly (variable entered as ratio, per paper's extraction), so not poolable with per-100 or index measures without rescaling.

paper_verdict.estimator_family: two-step system GMM (Tables 3, 5); dynamic panel quantile regression, Powell 2016 (Table 4)
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: ICT is a sum of fixed telephone, mobile and internet subscriptions per 100 people (logged), a composite measure. Models 2-4 and 6-8 give ICT main effects conditional on interactions. Table 3 and Table 5 estimates and the Table 4 quantile estimates come from the same sample (1,219 obs, 84 countries) so are not independent; Table 5 repeats Table 3 with population growth. Table 4 outcome is labelled 'D.var LP' and its coefficients (about 0.002-0.009) are on a different scale from GMM (about 0.015) so mixing estimator types needs care. Reverse causality is addressed only through GMM internal instruments (no specific discussion). Income group is middle-income (46 upper-middle, 38 lower-middle).
